classification_rationale: Not a missing-doc finding under the six-item list and not wording; a repo-hygiene observation about a file this change touches. Recorded so the headroom measurement is on record.

summary: Wording-only improvement to the 411 operator-facing remediation text. Meaning is unambiguous; cosmetic.

trigger: any edit to the /mcp/ row in kBodyCapTable
summary: The /mcp/ table row is INERT. server.cpp:7533's is_mcp_path() branch returns before resolve_body_cap() (called at :7673 in the else-if), so MCP's enforced cap is mcp::kMcpMaxRequestBodyBytes, not the table. Editing the /mcp/ row changes the published doc table and metric seeding and nothing else - a silent no-op on a security control. The routed-concerns row asserts the table IS the single chokepoint. I6 raise (a) FALSE ASSURANCE applies. Confirmed independently by the orchestrator at server.cpp:7533/7552/7556 vs :7673.
classification_rationale: The routed-concern row and the table's own header assert a single-chokepoint property the code does not provide for the /mcp/ class.

trigger: any mutating route registered on the web_server_-> receiver, or in a .inc file
summary: The completeness guard is blind on TWO independent axes. (1) Its regex is \b(sink|svr)\.(Post|Put|Patch)\( but server.cpp and two .inc files register via web_server_->; measured 39 invisible registrations against 137 seen (22% of a 176-route surface), concentrated in the very file this change edits - architect measured 33, orchestrator re-measured 39. (2) read_all_cpp_files() filters extension()==".cpp", so deployment_discovery_routes.inc (2) and directory_patch_routes.inc (4) are invisible for a SECOND reason the architect did not reach - found by the orchestrator during verification. The test header claims a route added anywhere is picked up automatically; that is false and will mislead the next author. quality-engineer's mutation test passed because it injected an svr.Post spelling the regex already handles, and confirmed the count by re-running the test's own regex - circular.
classification_rationale: Test header and commit message both assert a completeness property the scan does not deliver; the false-green risk is the point of the guard.

trigger: unauthenticated GET /api/v1/devices with Content-Length: 104857600, or Transfer-Encoding: chunked
summary: GET/HEAD are excluded from the cap on a FALSE premise. The in-code justification says they never carry a body; httplib.h:8334-8338 expect_content() returns true for ANY method with Content-Length>0 or chunked framing, and this repo's own web_utils.hpp:546-548 already documents the opposite for the MCP branch. Verified empirically with a harness against the vendored header: pre-routing ran with the Content-Length in hand and 20 MiB was still buffered on a GET. The change therefore ships the pre-auth buffering hole it exists to close, still open on every GET/HEAD path, with a recorded justification that will stop the next reviewer re-checking it.
classification_rationale: Comment asserts library behaviour that is false and that the repo documents correctly elsewhere; adjacent to the enforcement branch.

trigger: every server-suite run; discover_mutating_routes() called from 3 TEST_CASEs plus a 4th independent read, no cache
summary: CONVERGENT: found independently by cpp-expert (F1), cross-platform (CP-1), performance (PERF-2) and build-ci (F2) in two separate waves - 4 independent reporters, the strongest signal this run produced. The source tree is read and std::regex-scanned 4x per process. Measured 8.2-8.5s on Linux -O2 and ~11.1s at -O0; cost is O(tree size) and unbounded on a growing tree. Windows shard B has timed out once before on this shape and MSVC std::regex is materially slower. One-line fix: function-local static const cache.

No admit-side denominator. Unlike the quota gate, which ships yuzu_server_principal_quota_admits_total precisely so the exhaustion RATE is computable server-side, the body cap gives only the numerator. A rise from 5 to 50 rejections/hour is uninterpretable - 10x more attack traffic or 10x more legitimate traffic against an unrealistic cap, and the operator cannot tell which.

No alert rule or documented threshold for the new counter. Compounds sre-A: the throttled log is unreliable for the low-volume legitimate-refusal case, leaving the metric as the only reliable signal, and nothing points an operator at it.

trigger: an operator's legitimate traffic exceeds a judgment-call cap in production
summary: No runtime override. Caps are constexpr; the documented remedy is edit-the-table-and-redeploy. Every sibling resource limit in this product (--max-sse-streams, --principal-max-concurrency, --principal-rate-limit) is a runtime flag. A resource control with no runtime escape hatch is an incident with no mitigation.

trigger: unresolved - coverage gap, no demonstrated defect
summary: No live end-to-end test of the NEW general pre-routing branch. Both new test files are unit tests over the table or a source-text scan; neither exercises server.cpp at runtime, and TestRouteSink by contract does not model pre-routing. Materially raised by this run: all three blocking findings (arch-F1, arch-F2, cppsafe-1) are wiring defects an httplib-backed test of the general branch would plausibly have caught.

trigger: a regex or extraction regression silently dropping routes
summary: REQUIRE(routes.size() > 50) tolerates losing 63% of the 137 routes it sees without failing. Compounds arch-F2: the floor is exactly what should have caught 39 invisible registrations and did not.

The four health-probe paths early-return Unhandled at server.cpp:7390, ABOVE the cap branch at :7656, so the cap never runs on them. These are also the only paths that skip the 401 gate, making them the LAST unauthenticated 100 MiB buffer in the server - exactly what #2407 exists to close. rest-api.md states 'Every request except GET/HEAD is checked', which is false. Confirmed by the orchestrator by reading both line ranges.
classification_rationale: Control asserted in docs/comments is not enforced on the named path.

trigger: POST /scim/v2/Users with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, or Content-Encoding: br
summary: CONVERGENT (security-guardian F2 + unhappy-path UP-1, independent waves). oversize = !unmeasurable && ... and requires_measurable is false for all 17 non-MCP rows, so ONE header falls the request through to httplib's 100 MiB backstop on every class. Worse: CPPHTTPLIB_BROTLI_SUPPORT is TRUE (orchestrator confirmed in httplibTargets.cmake:61 and 424 build.ninja refs; ZLIB and ZSTD are OFF), and httplib bounds only the DECOMPRESSED size, so Content-Encoding: br is ~1000x amplification from a tiny wire body. The shipped control binds only well-behaved clients. Separable zero-compat half: refuse non-identity Content-Encoding for all classes - no Yuzu route accepts a compressed request body.
classification_rationale: Control asserted in docs/comments is not enforced on the named path.

trigger: pipelined POST to a 4 KiB-capped route with a body exceeding the cap, plus a smuggled request line
summary: Keep-alive connection-reuse constraint on the pre-routing reject path. Mechanism, deployment preconditions and candidate remediations are REDACTED here and tracked through private security reporting per SECURITY.md — this repo is public and docs/agents/issue-standard.md §6 requires an exploitable defect to go private, treating the doubtful case as exploitable. Pre-existing for /mcp/ since #2437; this change widens the affected surface from one route class to roughly eighteen.
classification_rationale: Control asserted in docs/comments is not enforced on the named path.

trigger: SCIM mutation >= 64 KiB, e.g. an Okta/Entra Group PATCH with ~1300+ members
summary: CONVERGENT (enterprise-readiness EIR-1 HIGH, architect F4 MEDIUM, unhappy-path UP-7 MEDIUM). The pre-routing cap for /scim/v2/ is byte-identical to the handler's own 64 KiB check but runs strictly earlier, so it always wins and the handler check is dead code. Every oversize SCIM request now gets a generic A4 envelope on application/json instead of RFC 7644 3.12 application/scim+json with schemas/status/detail. Both rest-api.md and server-admin.md claim SCIM sees 'no behavior change, only an earlier rejection' - false for this class. Real trigger is well inside the 5000-member ceiling the code otherwise permits.
classification_rationale: Control asserted in docs/comments is not enforced on the named path.

trigger: any POST /api/dashboard/tar-execute with a near-limit SQL query, especially one containing quotes or newlines
summary: CONVERGENT (consistency-auditor C-1 HIGH + happy-path MEDIUM, independent waves). The cap measures the RAW body at 4096 while dashboard_routes.cpp:866 measures the form-DECODED sql at 4096. Raw body is sql= plus percent-encoded(sql) plus a companion scope= field, so a 4093-4096 char query is unconditionally rejected and anything containing a quote, paren or newline far earlier - one reviewer measured a 4085-char realistic query producing a 5078-byte body, 24% over. rest-api.md claims it Matches the handler own check exactly and server-admin.md lists TAR queries among routes whose clients see no behavior change; both false. The table comment explicitly DECLINES the form-encoding margin that its two sibling dashboard classes already carry - that is the root cause.
classification_rationale: Published doc asserts parity with a handler check that the code does not provide, on a route the upgrade note names as unaffected.

trigger: POST /api/instructions/import with responseTemplates supplied as a native JSON array rather than a string
summary: kMaxImportTemplateStringBytes (256 KiB) is checked at :932 INSIDE the is_string() branch at :930; the native-array branch at :917 has no size check at all, so responseTemplates as a JSON array is unbounded. Surfaced in passing by the fix agent while sizing the instruction_import cap, then verified independently by the orchestrator. PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by #2407 - and #2407 materially improves it, since the new 16 MiB instruction_import cap now bounds the whole body where previously only httplib 100 MB did. Worth its own issue as an asymmetry in the import path. Derivation is the recorder reading the code, not the reporter stating a band.
classification_rationale: A guard named for a size limit applies to only one of two shapes of the same field.
